summary: The denominator alignment is internally careful, but the new result-defining sample remains outside a complete, verified replication pipeline: it is built and copied manually, while the committed manifest still describes the superseded 17-input run. The Old/New middle-initial comparison also changes the validator, so it cannot by itself identify improved linkage quality even though the captions now disclose the convention.

findings.title: The new denominator artifact is manually transferred and absent from the current input manifest
findings.what_the_code_does: The builder saves `linkage_sample1940.dta` to machine A's `$REP_SNU/.../DATA/INTERMEDIATE` and instructs the author to copy it to machine B's `$D_FLAGS`; the only runner is an untracked, hardcoded wrapper. Machine B now preflights that copied file, and the hashing script expects 15 inputs, but `input_manifest_machineB.md` still records 17 inputs, includes the three superseded files, and contains no hash for `linkage_sample1940.dta`.
findings.why_it_matters: The current documented `python replication/hash_inputs_machineB.py --check` must report the new sample as changed or new, so the regenerated Tables 5–8 cannot pass the repository's frozen-input integrity check. An external replicator also cannot produce the defining denominator artifact through either master pipeline without discovering and performing an undocumented cross-machine transfer.
findings.how_to_check: Run `python -c "import replication.hash_inputs_machineB as h; print('\n'.join(h.input_list()))"` and compare its 15 paths with `replication/input_manifest_machineB.md`; then run `rg -n "build_linkage_sample1940|linkage_sample1940" replication LINKAGE/code` to confirm that no tracked master invokes the builder or performs the transfer.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the builder to the machine-A master, script a checksummed transfer into machine B's expected path, and regenerate `replication/input_manifest_machineB.md` on machine B so it contains the 15 active inputs and the new file's SHA-256 before accepting regenerated tables.

findings.title: The Old/New MI comparison changes the validator as well as the linked pairs
findings.what_the_code_does: For Old links, `miv` is `mi_anc`; for New links it is `mi_ml`. The code then computes `count if mi1930 == mi1940` and presents the resulting rates side by side as `MI Match Rate (%)` in a panel titled `Coverage and Link Quality`. Thus both the candidate links and the 1940 initial against which they are evaluated change between columns.
findings.why_it_matters: A higher New rate can result from the model re-transcribing the 1940 middle initial differently even when the linked pair is unchanged. The revised captions disclose the own-initial convention, but the row still cannot be interpreted as an isolated improvement in link quality; a referee will require a fixed-validator comparison for that claim.
findings.how_to_check: Run `replication/diagnostics/validation_fixed_initials.do`, then score the ABE, JW, and HLINK Old/New pairs twice—once using `mi_anc` for both versions and once using `mi_ml` for both—and compare those changes with the reported own-initial changes.
findings.suggested_fix: Report a fixed-validator MI rate as the link-quality comparison, preferably alongside the disclosed own-transcription rate. At minimum, rename the existing row and panel so they do not characterize its Old/New difference as independent linkage validation.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so claims-vs-code review was limited to generated table labels, captions, and source comments; prose claims could not be checked.

The external census, linkage, and truth datasets were unavailable, and the Stata pipeline could not be run. Record counts and runtime behavior are therefore source-based except where Python-only checks were possible.
This was a working-tree diff review, not a comprehensive audit of the pre-existing linkage and truth-set construction code.
The independence, coverage, and error properties of the asserted truth links and middle-initial sources could not be empirically assessed without the underlying data.
